ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure: It is known that the length of line segment $AB=16\,\text{cm}$, point $N$ is on the line segment $AB$, $NB=3\,\text{cm}$, $M$ is the midpoint of $AB$. If there is a point $C$ on the line segment $AB$ satisfying $BC=10\,\text{cm}$, find the length of line segment $MC$.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since there exists a point $C$ on line segment $AB$, and $BC=10\,\text{cm}$, \\
it follows that $MC=BC-MB=10-8=\boxed{2}\,\text{cm}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached diagram shows a single horizontal line segment with A at the left endpoint and B at the right endpoint. Points M and N lie on the segment between A and B, in the order A--M--N--B, with M to the left of N and B at the right end. Reasoning: From the text, AB = 16 cm and M is the midpoint of AB, so MB = 16 ÷ 2 = 8 cm. The point C is on segment AB and satisfies BC = 10 cm. Since BC = 10 cm is greater than BM = 8 cm, C must lie to the left of M on the segment. Therefore MC is the difference between BC and BM: MC = 10 - 8 = 2 cm.
